page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the N2 family. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware. The underlying processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES cryptography, and Intel Virtualization Technology.

Synthetic benchmarks indicate that the n2-standard-2 occupies the lower tiers of performance. The instance achieved a single-core Geekbench score of 1123.0 and a multi-core score of 1333.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with large-block read and write speeds measured at 13.8 GB/sec and 11.79 GB/sec respectively, both placing in the bottom 10% of tested systems. However, single-threaded gzip compression performance is a relative strength, registering an average result of 23.81 GB/sec.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the n2-standard-2 is positioned for low-intensity workloads. It is suitable for basic web serving, where it demonstrated a static throughput of 1.95 GB/sec, or lightweight database operations, scoring 731.04 on Passmark database tests. With Redis SET operations reaching 1.72 million operations per second, it can support small-scale caching layers. The instance offers a predictable, dedicated CPU allocation for entry-level general-purpose tasks without the variable performance of burstable instances, making it a stable option for development environments and minor utility services.
